item.title: What Is at Stake in Hungary’s Election?
item.description: Hungary’s April election could end Viktor Orbán’s 16-year rule as opposition leader Peter Magyar mounts a serious challenge. The outcome will shape Hungary’s democratic trajectory and impact the European Union’s unity and policy for years to come.

item.title: Iran’s Real War Is Against the Global Economy
item.description: EST President Navin Girishankar argues that Iran may be losing the military contest with the United States, but it is fighting a different war—one aimed at the global economy.

item.title: The Wars After the War: Why Israel and Iran May Keep Fighting
item.description: Even after the latest war with Iran ends, lower-level hostilities between Iran and Israel—and perhaps the United States—might continue.

item.title: What Can the United States and Israel Accomplish in Iran?
item.description: Secretary Hegseth called Operation Epic Fury “straightforward.” But while the United States strikes the Iranian navy, nuclear program, and missiles, Israel and Trump eye regime change. This piece deconstructs that daylight and the true cost of each goal.

item.title: Chokepoint: How the War with Iran Threatens Global Food Security
item.description: The war with Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint in global oil, natural gas, and fertilizer trade. CSIS experts examine the immediate impacts on farmers and markets—and the long-term risks to food security if shipping does not resume.

item.title: States Weekly: March 11, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers March 11, 2026.

item.title: Unpacking Iran’s Drone Campaign in the Gulf: Early Lessons for Future Drone Warfare
item.description: Kateryna Bondar analyzes Iran’s drone retaliation campaign during Operation Epic Fury, showing how mass one-way attack drones are reshaping air warfare and what lessons the United States can draw from both the Gulf conflict and Ukraine’s experience.
